title: Democratic Preference Alignment via Sortition-Weighted RLHF
benchmark_measurement: Using religious affiliation as one of seven demographic quota constraints to construct a representative panel of human raters for preference-based fine-tuning. The goal was to align model behavior with the values of a demographically representative public, not to measure knowledge or bias related to religion itself.
findings: The paper found that enforcing demographic representativeness during training, using religion as one of seven key demographic attributes for creating a representative panel, yielded models whose behavior better reflected values elicited from a representative public. There were no specific findings about religious groups or religion-specific model behavior, as religion was used as a structural variable for data sampling and weighting rather than a topic for evaluation.
